Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

A linear map $T:V\to W$ ([[def-linear-map]]) between inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) is a **linear isometry** if

$$\lVert Tv\rVert=\lVert v\rVert$$

for every $v\in V$, where the norm is the induced norm [[def-inner-product-norm]]. An invertible linear isometry from a real finite-dimensional inner product space to itself is an **orthogonal operator**; over $\mathbb C$ it is a **unitary operator**.

Equivalently, once the finite-dimensional characterisation is proved, orthogonal and unitary operators are the endomorphisms satisfying $T^*T=TT^*=I$.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

derivations.claim: If $m=0$, both products are $I$, so their difference is zero and the empty sum is zero. This is the claimed bound in the empty case.

If the Hilbert space is zero-dimensional, its unique endomorphism has norm zero, so the product difference is zero and the bound holds. Otherwise, for $m\ge1$, insert and subtract mixed products to obtain $U_m\cdots U_1-V_m\cdots V_1 =\sum_{j=1}^m U_m\cdots U_{j+1}(U_j-V_j)V_{j-1}\cdots V_1.$ Expansion cancels adjacent terms and leaves exactly the left side. Each outer product is unitary and has norm one by [F1]; [F2] and the unitary invariance derived there show that each summand has norm at most $\epsilon_j$. The operator-norm triangle inequality then gives the stated sum.

$$D(P_u,P_v)\le \|u-v\|.$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **trace distance** is
$$D(\rho,\sigma):=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). The factor $1/2$ is part of this state-distance convention. The diamond norm below is an unhalved norm on maps.

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. Then

$$\|A\|_1=\max\{\,|\operatorname{tr}_H(B^*A)|: B:H\to K\text{ linear and }\|B\|\le1\,\}.$$

Consequently, on the vector space of linear maps $H\to K$, the trace norm is
nonnegative, absolutely homogeneous, definite, and satisfies the triangle
inequality.

$$\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}|p_a-q_a|\le D(\rho,\sigma).$$
The two-effect projective measurement from the Holevo–Helstrom theorem attains equality.

Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel $c\subset a\otimes b$, let $i_{ab}^c:c\to a\otimes b$ be the
standard unit-vector isometric inclusion. Since the multiplicity space is
$V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$, its orthonormal basis vector is
the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary fusion category, let $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$
be the representative set fixed in [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]], and take
$a_1,\ldots,a_n,d\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$. Fix any parenthesized
binary tree $T$ on the ordered input list. The fusion-tree vectors of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]] form an orthonormal basis of
$\operatorname{Hom}(T,d)$. For $n\ge2$, their number is

$$m_T(d)=\sum_{\substack{\ell\text{ admissible, with every internal label in }\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)}}\;\prod_{v\,\mathrm{internal}}N_{\ell(v_L)\,\ell(v_R)}^{\ell(v)},$$

where the sum runs over charge labelings only (the product counts the
vertex multiplicity indices), the leaves carry the inputs, the root carries
$d$, and each internal edge is labeled by a representative simple charge.
For the empty tree, $m_0(d)=1$ if $d=\mathbf1$ and $0$ otherwise; for one
input, $m_1(d)=1$ if $a_1=d$ and $0$ otherwise. The left-associated tree on
$n\ge2$ inputs satisfies

$$m_n(d)=\sum_e m_{n-1}(e)N_{e a_n}^d\qquad(n\ge2).$$

Fix a unitary fusion category $\mathcal D$ and the representative set
$\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$ of [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]].
For an ordered list $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$,
$n\ge1$, a total charge $c\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal D)$, and a
parenthesized input tensor $T$, let $V=\operatorname{Hom}(T,c)\ne0$,
equipped with that definition's orthonormal fusion-tree inner product.
The identical-input case $x_1=\cdots=x_n=x$ retains the notation
$V=V(x^n\to c)$. Let
$\mathcal C=\mathbb C^k$ with its ordered orthonormal computational basis,
where $k\ge1$. A **fixed-charge encoding** is an isometry
$J:\mathcal C\to V$, so $J^*J=I_{\mathcal C}$. Its code subspace is
$J\mathcal C$, and its code projector is
$$P:=JJ^*:V\to V.$$
An encoding records a chosen subspace of a fusion space; it does not identify
that subspace with an object of the fusion category.

Every F-symbol matrix in orthonormal fusion-tree bases of a unitary fusion
category is unitary.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary fusion category and fix a set
$\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ of representatives for the simple
isomorphism classes, with the tensor unit $\mathbf1$ itself representing its
class. Throughout this definition, the ordered input charges
$a_1,\ldots,a_n$, total charge $d$, and all internal edge charges are labels
in $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$. Also fix a parenthesized binary fusion
tree. At each internal vertex with incoming charges $x,y$ and outgoing charge
$z$, choose one vector from an orthonormal basis of $V_{xy}^z$. An
**admissible labeling** assigns a representative charge to each internal edge
so that each chosen vertex basis is nonempty; a separate multiplicity-basis
index is retained at every vertex. Compose the vertex morphisms, inserting the
associators required by the chosen tree, to obtain a morphism from the
parenthesized input tensor to $d$. These composite morphisms are the
**fusion-tree vectors**. The family is called a **fusion-tree basis** when it
is an orthonormal basis of the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space. For the
empty input list the tensor is $\mathbf1$ and its empty tree vector is
$\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$ when $d=\mathbf1$; for one input $a_1$, the
only tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{a_1}$ when $d=a_1$. The next local
lemma proves the basis property for every finite input list and includes the
dimension recursion ([[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]).

Fix a unitary braided fusion category $\mathcal C$ and the simple-object
representative set $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ used in
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. Let $x,c\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$,
let $n\ge2$, and suppose $V(x^n\to c)\ne0$. Use the left-associated fusion-tree basis. For the Artin
generator $\sigma_i$ that exchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st strands, let
$T_i$ be the specified sequence of $F$-moves that changes from the fixed tree
basis to a basis where those two charges fuse first, and let $R_i$ apply the
corresponding $R$-symbol on each pair-charge channel. Define
$$\rho_c(\sigma_i):=T_i^{-1}R_iT_i.$$
This defines the generator assignment. The next theorem proves that the
assignment descends from words to a well-defined group homomorphism. Word
products use matrix multiplication acting right-to-left on column vectors.
The abstract group in this definition is the Artin group
[[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]; the positive crossing is the
generator convention used for the displayed $R$-symbols. If a motion is
described chronologically, its matrix product is written in reverse temporal
order.

For a unitary braided fusion category $\mathcal C$, simple representatives
$x,c\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ as in
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]], $n\ge2$, and a nonzero fixed-total fusion
space, the operators in
[[def-qc-tqc-braid-action-from-fusion-data]] define a unitary group
homomorphism
$$\rho_c:B_n\longrightarrow U(V(x^n\to c)).$$
In particular, the adjacent Artin relations and distant commutation relations
hold in each fixed-charge block.

Every F-symbol matrix in orthonormal fusion-tree bases of a unitary fusion
category is unitary.

derivations.claim: In the grouped tree, choose an admissible local fusion-tree basis vector $f_i\in V(\tau^3\to a_i)$ for each triple and a basis vector $g\in V(a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n\to c)$ for the outer fusion. The composites obtained by inserting $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ into $g$ are exactly the grouped fusion-tree vectors. By completeness and orthonormality [F1], their orthogonal direct sum over $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is the full grouped fusion space, which gives the displayed tensor/direct-sum decomposition.

A braid word supported inside triple $i$ changes only the local morphism $f_i$, by $f_i\mapsto f_i\circ b^{-1}$ under [F2]; every $f_j$ with $j\ne i$ and the outer morphism $g$ are unchanged. Rebracketing to the fixed tree conjugates this matrix by the unitary in [F3], proving the same operator statement in that convention. Tensoring an operator $A$ with an identity does not increase its norm: expand a vector in an orthonormal basis of the spectator factor and sum $\|A\xi_j\|^2\le\|A\|^2\sum\|\xi_j\|^2$. The norm of a finite orthogonal direct sum is at most the maximum of its block norms by the same squared-norm decomposition. These finite identities justify uniform spectator bounds.

Let $H$ be a fixed finite fusion space with an orthonormal fusion-tree basis
in the category and simple-representative domain of
[[def-qa-37-fusion-input-encoding]]. For a colored task, $H$ is the
currently occupied ordered-list summand tracked by the task record.
For an adjacent pair of leaves or a declared adjacent pair of subtrees, recouple
the tree by its specified unitary $F$-moves so that the pair fuses first. For
each allowed simple total charge $a$ of that pair, let $P_a$ be the orthogonal
projection onto the span of basis vectors whose pair label is $a$, transported
back by the inverse recoupling unitary. Distinct channel subspaces are
orthogonal and their direct sum is $H$, so $(P_a)_a$ is a finite projective
measurement in the sense of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]]. Its outcome is
$a$, its unnormalized branch vector on input $\psi$ is $P_a\psi$, and the
recoupling follows the inverse-precomposition F convention of
[[def-qc-tqc-f-symbol]], whose unitarity is proved in
[[thm-qc-tqc-f-symbol-unitary]]. The branch vector is unnormalized until its probability is checked.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Two nonzero vectors $x,y\in H$ represent the same **ray** when $y=\alpha x$ for some nonzero $\alpha\in\mathbb C$. A **pure state** is such a ray. If $u$ is a unit representative, its associated operator is $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$, with the bra, ket and outer-product convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. The theorem [[thm-qc-ray-projector-well-defined-and-bijective]] proves that this operator is a rank-one orthogonal projection independent of the chosen unit representative, so it is the operator representative of the pure state.

Every pure-state ray projector on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space is a density operator. Conversely, every rank-one density operator is the projector of a unique pure-state ray.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator and $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ a finite projective measurement on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$. Put $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$. If $p_a>0$, then

$$\rho_a:=\frac{P_a\rho P_a}{p_a}$$

is a density operator whose image $\operatorname{im}(\rho_a):=\{\rho_a x:x\in H\}$ is contained in $\operatorname{im}(P_a)$ ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]). This statement assigns a conditional state only on positive-probability branches.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

For a vector $v$ in a real or complex inner product space, define its **inner-product norm** by

$$\lVert v\rVert:=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}.$$

Positive definiteness in [[def-inner-product-space]] makes the radicand a nonnegative real, and [[thm-nth-roots-exist]] supplies its unique nonnegative square root. The notation therefore defines one real number $\lVert v\rVert\ge0$. Its norm axioms are established in [[cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm]].

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with ordered
orthonormal bases $E=(e_j)_{j<n}$ and $F=(f_i)_{i<m}$. Let $T:H\to K$ be
linear ([[def-linear-map]]), and write $T_{ij}$ for the $(i,j)$ entry of its
matrix in these bases.
Then, for every $z\in H$,

$$Tz=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}\langle z,e_j\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}f_i, \qquad T=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}|f_i\rangle\langle e_j|.$$

For $x\in K$ and $y\in H$, the rank-one map $|x\rangle\langle y|$ has
coordinate matrix $[x]_F[y]_E^\dagger$, where $M^\dagger=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$.
Its amplitude satisfies
$\langle x|T|y\rangle_D=\langle Ty,x\rangle_{K,\mathrm{root}}$.
All sums are empty when an index dimension is zero, and the identities include
those cases.

derivations.claim: Set $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$, a density operator by [F3]. The Dirac rule and $P_a=P_a^*=P_a^2$ give $|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|P_a=|\psi\rangle\langle P_a\psi|$, whose trace is $\langle\psi,P_a\psi\rangle_{\rm root}$ by [F6]. By self-adjointness and idempotence this equals $\langle P_a\psi,P_a\psi\rangle_{\rm root}=\|P_a\psi\|^2$ by [F5]. Thus [F2] identifies $p_a=\|P_a\psi\|^2\ge0$ as the outcome probability. The resolution identity gives $\sum_a p_a=\langle\psi,(\sum_aP_a)\psi\rangle_{\rm root}=\|\psi\|^2=1$.

If $p_a>0$, then $\rho_a=P_a\rho P_a/p_a$ is the conditional density operator by [F4]. The Dirac rule and self-adjointness give $P_a\rho P_a=|P_a\psi\rangle\langle P_a\psi|$; using step 1.1, $\rho_a$ is the rank-one projector of the unit vector $P_a\psi/\sqrt{p_a}$. If $p_a=0$, step 1.1 gives $\|P_a\psi\|=0$, hence $P_a\psi=0$. The zero-probability convention is that this branch is omitted and no normalized conditional vector or state is assigned; division by $\sqrt{p_a}=0$ is undefined.

Fix the Fibonacci convention with common exchange scalar $R_1$. Let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be exponent sum, sending each Artin generator $\sigma_i$
to $1$. If $\widetilde\rho$ is the generator-normalized representation
$\widetilde\rho(\sigma_i)=R_1^{-1}\rho(\sigma_i)$, then for every braid $b$
and every total-charge block,
$$\rho(b)=R_1^{e(b)}\widetilde\rho(b).$$
The scalar is the same on every total-charge block and every spectator
multiplicity. It is a global phase for an uncontrolled fixed-sector
computation; under coherent control it is a relative phase and must be
tracked.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with the root pairing linear in the first argument. For nonzero $x\in H$, put $u=x/\|x\|$. If $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ has $|\lambda|=1$, then $u$ and $\lambda u$ determine the same rank-one density operator. Consequently, for every finite POVM $(E_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ on $H$, each defined outcome probability satisfies

$$\operatorname{tr}(|u\rangle\langle u|E_a)=\operatorname{tr}(|\lambda u\rangle\langle\lambda u|E_a).$$

The unnormalized vector $x$ itself gives $\operatorname{tr}(|x\rangle\langle x|)=\|x\|^2$ and is not a density operator when $\|x\|\ne1$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and $U:H\to H$ a unitary. Let $\theta\in\mathbb R$, and suppose the model separately grants controlled access to both $U$ and $e^{i\theta}U$. There is a normalized eigenvector $\phi$ with $U\phi=\mu\phi$ and $|\mu|=1$. Let $C=Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the control qubit with ordered computational basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$; define $|\pm\rangle=(|0\rangle\pm|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and prepare $(|0\rangle+\overline\mu|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with target $\phi$. Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to1)\oplus V(\tau^6\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^5\oplus\mathbb C^8$,
the closure in $U(5)\times U(8)$ contains $SU(5)\times SU(8)$.

Fix $d\in\{2,5,8\}$ and put
$$SU(d)=\{T\in M_d(\mathbb C):T^*T=I_d,\ \det T=1\}.$$
A **certified $SU(d)$ matrix input** is an exact target $T\in SU(d)$ together
with a deterministic Cauchy-name procedure which, on unary input $1^b$ for
$b\ge1$, returns a rational complex matrix $Q_b$ such that each real and
imaginary coordinate of each entry differs from the corresponding coordinate
of $T$ by at most $2^{-b}$. The interface also specifies a worst-case bit-time
bound $t(b)$ for the query. A **polynomial-time name** has
$t(b)\le(b+1)^c$ for some fixed integer $c\ge1$. The target is the matrix
specified by the entire Cauchy name; if two targets satisfy these bounds for the same sequence $(Q_b)_{b\ge1}$,
every coordinate difference is at most $2^{1-b}$ for all $b$, hence is zero.
No individual $Q_b$ is required to be unitary or special unitary. A requested tolerance is a positive binary
rational and its numerator/denominator encoding length is recorded
separately. For $d=2$ this specializes the unary-name convention of
[[def-qc-effective-unitary-matrix-input]]. For $d=5,8$ it is the same
entrywise interface in the fixed block dimensions; no dimension is input to
an algorithm as an unbounded parameter.

**Inputs:** certified Cauchy names for targets $T_5\in SU(5)$ and
$T_8\in SU(8)$; a positive binary-rational tolerance $\varepsilon$; and the
fixed normalized six-strand Fibonacci B6 generators in both total-charge
blocks. Use the ordered alphabet
$(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_5,\sigma_1^{-1},\ldots,\sigma_5^{-1})$ for $B_6$.
For $d\in\{5,8\}$, form the exact generators
$B_i^{(d)}=rI+(1-r)P_i^{(d)}$ from the Fibonacci path-projector formula
[[lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-b6-path-projectors-and-artin]], and use
$(B_i^{(d)})^*$ for inverse letters. To produce a rational approximant to a
word block at precision $p$, write $b=a_1\cdots a_\ell$ in Artin product
order and multiply its exact letter matrices as
$B_{a_1}^{(d)}\cdots B_{a_\ell}^{(d)}$ (the rightmost factor acts first).
Write $q=\sqrt5>0$, $\phi=(1+q)/2$,
$s=\sqrt\phi>0$, $h=\sqrt{10+2q}>0$, and
$r=-(2\phi)^{-1}-ih/4$, the fixed Fibonacci data of
[[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]]. Start with dyadic root intervals $[2,3]$ for
$q$, $[1,2]$ for $s$, and $[3,4]$ for $h$. At each pass $t=1,2,\ldots$,
bisect each interval once, keeping the half certified by its defining square
equation and exact rational comparisons. To compare a rational midpoint square
for $s$ or $h$, refine the $q$ interval until the resulting rational enclosure
of its radicand lies strictly on one side; these radicands are irrational, so
each comparison terminates. For real intervals $I=[a,b]$ and
$J=[c,d]$, use $I+J=[a+c,b+d]$, $-I=[-b,-a]$,
$IJ=[\min(ac,ad,bc,bd),\max(ac,ad,bc,bd)]$, and
$I/J=I[1/d,1/c]$ when $0<c\le d$. Represent a complex enclosure by a pair

$(I_1J_1-I_2J_2,I_1J_2+I_2J_1)$; conjugation sends $(I_1,I_2)$ to
$(I_1,-I_2)$. Use these rational endpoint operations to evaluate each exact
matrix-entry expression. Stop when every real and imaginary coordinate
interval has width at most $2^{1-p}$, and return its midpoint;
the coordinate error is then at most $2^{-p}$. These intervals converge to
the exact entries, and all divisions are by positive powers of $\phi>1$, so

$\ell=0,\ldots,s_0$ in lexicographic order and precisions $1\le p\le s_0$

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Then
$$\|U_T(s)P(0)U_T(s)^*-P(s)\|\le A_m(s).$$

$$F=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\ \phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}.$$

For a finite adiabatic braid input with rank-$m$ spectral band and schedule
$T>0$, define
$$A_m(s)=\frac1T\left[\frac{m\|H'(0)\|}{g(0)^2} +\frac{m\|H'(s)\|}{g(s)^2} +\int_0^s\left(\frac{m\|H''(r)\|}{g(r)^2} +\frac{7m\sqrt m\|H'(r)\|^2}{g(r)^3}\right)dr\right].$$
Then
$\|U_T(s)P(0)U_T(s)^*-P(s)\|\le A_m(s)$, and every unit initial band
vector has leakage probability at most $A_m(s)^2$. In particular,
$\|[I-P(1)]U_T(1)A_0\|_{\rm op}\le A_m(1)$ and leakage probability is at
most $A_m(1)^2$. This result does not prove the separate in-band transport
condition or identify band transport with Fibonacci $F/R$ data.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $u,v\in H$ be unit vectors. Write $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$ and $P_v=|v\rangle\langle v|$ using the Dirac convention of [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]], and define their trace distance by $D(P_u,P_v):=\tfrac12\|P_u-P_v\|_1$, where $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the trace norm of [[def-qc-trace-norm]]. Then
$$D(P_u,P_v)\le \|u-v\|.$$

Let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\{E_a\}_{a\in\mathcal A}$ be any finite POVM. If $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)$ and $q_a=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma E_a)$, then
$$\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}|p_a-q_a|\le D(\rho,\sigma).$$
The two-effect projective measurement from the Holevo–Helstrom theorem attains equality.

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. Then

$$\|A\|_1=\max\{\,|\operatorname{tr}_H(B^*A)|: B:H\to K\text{ linear and }\|B\|\le1\,\}.$$

Consequently, on the vector space of linear maps $H\to K$, the trace norm is
nonnegative, absolutely homogeneous, definite, and satisfies the triangle
inequality.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

Assume the Fibonacci fusion rules
$1\otimes x=x\otimes1=x$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$, with each
listed summand of multiplicity one. For six ordered $\tau$ charges, let
$W_a$ be the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space of total charge
$a\in\{1,\tau\}$ in the tree that first fuses leaves $1,2,3$ and $4,5,6$
separately, then fuses those triple outputs. Let
$V_a$ be the same fixed-charge space in the left-associated tree.

To identify these spaces, write
$A=((\tau_1\otimes\tau_2)\otimes\tau_3)$. Use the object associator
composite
$$g=(\alpha^{-1}_{A\otimes\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6}) \circ\alpha^{-1}_{A,\tau_4,\tau_5\otimes\tau_6} \circ(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\alpha_{\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6})$$
from the triple-grouped input tree to the left-associated tree. On a fusion
morphism $f$ into $a$, define $G_a(f)=f\circ g^{-1}:V_a$; this is a unitary
change of fusion-tree coordinates.

For one triple of total charge $\tau$, its two orthonormal path vectors are
indexed by the charge $x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two anyons: both
$x\otimes\tau\to\tau$ channels have multiplicity one. Write these vectors as
$|x\rangle$. For $x,y\in\{1,\tau\}$ and $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, let $|x,y;a\rangle$
be the grouped-tree vector with first triple path $x$, first triple total
$\tau$, second triple path $y$, second triple total $\tau$, and final vertex
channel $\tau\otimes\tau\to a$. The last channel has multiplicity one. Define
$$\mathcal C_a:=G_a\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{|x,y;a\rangle: x,y\in\{1,\tau\}\}\bigr)\subseteq V_a.$$
In the ordered basis
$(G_a|1,1;a\rangle,G_a|1,\tau;a\rangle,
G_a|\tau,1;a\rangle,G_a|\tau,\tau;a\rangle)$, the inclusion
$J_a:\mathbb C^4\to V_a$ is an isometry; its code projector is $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$.
The same ordered local triple paths are used for $a=1$ and $a=\tau$; only
the final pair-charge coordinate differs. The orthogonal complements are
called leakage spaces.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For the normalized simultaneous six-$\tau$
Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to1)\oplus V(\tau^6\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^5\oplus\mathbb C^8$,
the closure in $U(5)\times U(8)$ contains $SU(5)\times SU(8)$.

Let $V=P V\oplus(I-P)V$ be an orthogonal decomposition of a finite-dimensional
Hilbert space, let $U$ and $W$ be unitary operators on the two summands, and
let $T:=U\oplus W$. If an ambient unitary $G$ satisfies
$\|G-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$, then the logical block error of $G$ relative
to $U$ and its leakage amplitude both are at most $\delta$.

Fix the Fibonacci convention with common exchange scalar $R_1$. Let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be exponent sum, sending each Artin generator $\sigma_i$
to $1$. If $\widetilde\rho$ is the generator-normalized representation
$\widetilde\rho(\sigma_i)=R_1^{-1}\rho(\sigma_i)$, then for every braid $b$
and every total-charge block,
$$\rho(b)=R_1^{e(b)}\widetilde\rho(b).$$
The scalar is the same on every total-charge block and every spectator
multiplicity. It is a global phase for an uncontrolled fixed-sector
computation; under coherent control it is a relative phase and must be
tracked.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every certified Cauchy input pair
$(T_5,T_8)\in SU(5)\times SU(8)$ and every positive rational
$\varepsilon$, the exhaustive compiler of
[[alg-qa-37-exhaustive-b6-block-pair-compiler]] halts with one six-strand
Fibonacci braid word whose normalized total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
matrices are each within operator norm $\varepsilon$ of $T_5,T_8$,
respectively. Density proves termination, but this result gives no useful
joint-block word-length or search-time bound.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

For a fixed inverse-closed dense $G\subset SU(2)$ and a certified base net of
radius $0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$ and a target $U\in SU(2)$, the level recursion
$\operatorname{Compile}(U,J)$ of
[[alg-qc-solovay-kitaev-unitary-compiler]] returns, for every real
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$, a word $W$ with
$\|U-W\|\le\varepsilon$, where $J$ is the least nonnegative integer
with $\eta_J\le\varepsilon$. For a real tolerance this means selecting
$J$ by ideal exact-real comparisons and calling the level subroutine
directly; the algorithm's top-level tolerance input is rational.
The level errors may be chosen as
$$\eta_j=64^{-2}(64^2\eta_0)^{(3/2)^j}.$$
The word length is at most $L_0 5^j$ at level $j$, hence
$O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$.
With shared recursive words, the exact-real arithmetic count is
$O(\log^{\log_{3/2}3}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{2.71}(1/\varepsilon))$;
printing the expanded word takes $O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$ time.
The latter are exact-real arithmetic bounds, not bit-complexity bounds.

Fix a finite inverse-closed dense $G\subset SU(2)$ whose real and imaginary
gate-entry coordinates are algebraic numbers supplied by their minimal
polynomials over $\mathbb Q$ and rational isolating intervals with opposite
endpoint signs and exactly one real root, and fix a
rational certified base-net radius
$0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$. Let the finite base-net certificate be fixed. Suppose
$U\in SU(2)$ is given by a Cauchy name whose query on unary input $1^b$ takes
at most $(b+1)^c$ bit operations for a fixed integer $c\ge1$. Given rational
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$ encoded as $\varepsilon=p/q$ by positive binary
integers $p,q$ with a fixed delimiter (not necessarily reduced), there is a
deterministic Turing implementation of the Solovay–Kitaev recursion that outputs a gate word $W$
with $\|U-W\|\le\varepsilon$ and length
$O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))$. If $s_\varepsilon$ is the binary
encoding length of $\varepsilon$ and
$N=\lceil\log_2(2/\varepsilon)\rceil$, its bit time, including reading
$\varepsilon$ and printing the expanded word, is
$$O\bigl((N+s_\varepsilon)^{c+10}\bigr).$$
Here $s_\varepsilon$ is the total bit length of this numerator/denominator
encoding. The constants depend on $G$, the fixed base-net certificate, and the fixed
algebraic descriptions. This is distinct from the exact-real arithmetic
count in [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-error-and-resource-bound]].

$$\frac{23}{48}4^n-\frac32 2^n+\frac43$$

This is a gate-count bound; it makes no numerical decomposition-time or finite-precision bit-complexity claim.

$L_0$. For every exact target $S\in SU(2)$ and rational
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$, let
$$\eta_{j+1}=64\eta_j^{3/2},\qquad J=\min\{j\ge0:\eta_j\le\varepsilon\}.$$
The ideal SK recursion returns a normalized braid word $W$ with
$\|S-W\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$ and length at most $L_0 5^J$; hence its
length is $O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$.
If each real and imaginary gate coordinate is supplied by its minimal
polynomial and rational isolating interval with the endpoint/root conditions
of the published finite-precision theorem, the base certificate is fixed,
and $S$ has a polynomial-time Cauchy name with query cost at most $(b+1)^c$,

$O((N+s_\varepsilon)^{c+10})$ from the cited theorem, where

Let $U_1,\ldots,U_m$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ be unitary operators on the same
finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and suppose
$\|U_j-V_j\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_j$ with $\epsilon_j\ge0$. With empty
products equal to the identity and empty sums equal to zero,
$$\|U_m\cdots U_1-V_m\cdots V_1\|_{\rm op} \le\sum_{j=1}^m\epsilon_j.$$

Let $n\ge1$ and $c\in\{1,\tau\}$ with $V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, using the
left-associated tree for both fixed-charge spaces. In the ordered list of
$3n$ Fibonacci $\tau$ charges, group consecutive leaves into $n$ triples;
within each triple fuse its first two charges and then its third, and fuse the
$n$ triple outputs by the left-associated $n$-leaf tree to total $c$. Restrict
each triple output to $\tau$; its two local paths are indexed by the charge
$x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two leaves. Fix a rebracketing sequence
of associators from this grouped tree to the fixed left-associated $3n$-leaf
tree, and let $R_{n,c}$ be the induced composite unitary. For each tensor
basis vector $e_{x_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{x_n}\otimes v_\lambda$, where
$e_1,e_\tau$ are the local triple paths and $v_\lambda$ is a basis vector of
$V(\tau^n\to c)$, map it to its grouped fusion-tree basis vector, then
apply $R_{n,c}$. Extend linearly and call the resulting map $J_{n,c}$. Its
image is the code $\mathcal C_{n,c}$ and it is an isometry; set
$P_{n,c}=J_{n,c}J_{n,c}^*$ for the code projector.
The factor $V(\tau^n\to c)$ retains all spectator fusion paths and is not a
physical preparation at zero cost.

Let $P$ be a code projection on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $V$. Let
$W_1,\ldots,W_G$ be ideal unitaries preserving $\operatorname{ran}P$, and let
$V_1,\ldots,V_G$ be physical unitaries with
$\|V_j-W_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_j$. If
$V_{\mathrm{tot}}=V_G\cdots V_1$ and $W_{\mathrm{tot}}=W_G\cdots W_1$,
then, with empty products equal to $I$ and empty sums equal to $0$,
$$\|V_{\mathrm{tot}}-W_{\mathrm{tot}}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le\sum_{j=1}^{G}\delta_j.$$
Consequently the logical block error and leakage amplitude relative to the
code action of $W_{\mathrm{tot}}$ are each at most $\sum_j\delta_j$.

Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel $c\subset a\otimes b$, let $i_{ab}^c:c\to a\otimes b$ be the
standard unit-vector isometric inclusion. Since the multiplicity space is
$V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$, its orthonormal basis vector is
the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

The **real numbers** are the quotient ring

$$\mathbb{R} := \mathcal{C} / \mathcal{N}$$

of the ring of Cauchy sequences ([[thm-cauchy-ring]]) by the ideal of null
sequences ([[lem-null-ideal]]).

The Cauchy-sequence reals $\mathbb{R}_C$ have the **least-upper-bound property**:
every nonempty $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_C$ that is bounded above has a least upper
bound $\sup S \in \mathbb{R}_C$. Hence, together with [[thm-reals-ordered-field]],
$\mathbb{R}_C$ is a **complete ordered field** ([[def-complete-ordered-field]]).

The **real numbers** are the quotient ring

$$\mathbb{R} := \mathcal{C} / \mathcal{N}$$

of the ring of Cauchy sequences ([[thm-cauchy-ring]]) by the ideal of null
sequences ([[lem-null-ideal]]).

The Cauchy-sequence reals $\mathbb{R}_C$ ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]]) are
**Archimedean** ([[def-archimedean-field]]): for every $x \in \mathbb{R}_C$
there is a natural number $n$ with $x < n \cdot 1$, where the canonical natural
$n \cdot 1$ is the class $\hat n$ of the constant rational sequence $n$.
Equivalently, the canonical naturals $(\hat n)_{n \ge 1}$ are cofinal.

derivations.claim: By [F6], the code consists of $n$ local two-path triple factors and the full spectator space. The fusion recurrence from [F9]–[F10] gives $m_2(1)=m_2(\tau)=1$, then $m_3(1)=m_2(\tau)=1$ and $m_3(\tau)=m_2(1)+m_2(\tau)=2$. Thus the local triple total-$\tau$ factor is two-dimensional and the total-$1$ factor is one-dimensional. If $U=I$, choose the empty target list and the empty braid proves the claim. For the rest of the proof suppose $U\ne I$. For $n\ge2$, [F1] gives a finite QSD list of one-qubit gates and CNOTs; for $n=1$, use $U$ as its one-qubit list. Replace each nonadjacent two-qubit target on wires $i<j$ by adjacent SWAPs carrying wire $j$ next to $i$, the target on that adjacent pair, and the reverse SWAPs. On each computational basis vector, conjugation by this wire permutation transfers the same two target coordinates and undoing the permutation restores the others; hence the replacement is exactly the original gate. The resulting finite list contains only one-qubit and adjacent two-qubit targets.

Let $M>0$ be the number of factors in the resulting list; positivity follows from $U\ne I$ in step 1.1. By [F14] choose an integer $N>\max\{2M/\epsilon,2/\eta_0\}$ and put $\delta=1/N$. Then $\delta<\epsilon/(2M)$ and $\delta<\eta_0/2$. For a one-qubit factor $G\in U(2)$ write $\det G=a+ib$; since $G$ is unitary, $a^2+b^2=1$. If $a=-1$, set $\alpha=i$; otherwise define $x=\sqrt{(1+a)/2},\qquad y=\operatorname{sgn}(b)\sqrt{(1-a)/2},\qquad \alpha=x+iy,$ with $\operatorname{sgn}(0)=1$. The roots exist by [F13], and direct squaring gives $\alpha^2=\det G$ and $|\alpha|=1$. Therefore $S=\alpha^{-1}G$ is unitary with determinant one. By [F2] and [A1], compile $S$ to a normalized braid word within $\delta$. If its Artin exponent sum is $k$, the physical action on the local total-$\tau$ code sector is within $\delta$ of $(R_1z^{-1})^k\alpha^{-1}G$.

For an adjacent two-qubit factor $G$, [F4] and [A1] give one normalized six-strand braid and a code-preserving ideal extension with full ambient operator error at most $\delta$, uniformly over all spectator fusion paths. If its exponent sum is $k$, [F8] multiplies both the physical word and ideal extension by the same scalar $R_1^k$; their norm error remains $\delta$ and the code target is $R_1^kG$. For a one-qubit word from step 2.1, use [F11]–[F12] to decompose the register by the selected triple's total charge and spectator fusion paths. On the two-dimensional total-$\tau$ sector define the ideal block to be the target $G$ times the phase $(R_1z^{-1})^k\alpha^{-1}$; on the one-dimensional total-$1$ sector define it to equal the physical braid. These blocks form a unitary preserving the code. Its full ambient norm difference from the physical word is at most $\delta$: the error is at most $\delta$ on the total-$\tau$ block by step 2.1 and zero on total charge $1$, and tensoring with spectator identities and taking an orthogonal direct sum does not increase the maximum block norm.

Each ideal extension preserves the code and its restriction to the code is the corresponding QSD factor multiplied by its recorded scalar. Their product therefore restricts to $\omega(U\otimes I_{V(\tau^n\to c)})$ for the product phase $\omega$. The physical/ideal factor errors are each at most $\delta$, so [F5] bounds the full product error by $M\delta<\epsilon/2$. Applying [F7] gives logical block error and leakage amplitude at most $M\delta<\epsilon$. For certified Cauchy target names [F3] guarantees that the B6 subsearch terminates; its density proof supplies no useful length or time cutoff. The only choice axiom is [A1], inherited from the density suppliers; all remaining arguments are finite-dimensional.

Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel $c\subset a\otimes b$, let $i_{ab}^c:c\to a\otimes b$ be the
standard unit-vector isometric inclusion. Since the multiplicity space is
$V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$, its orthonormal basis vector is
the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

Let $(P_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}$ be the finite fusion-channel projectors of
[[def-qa-37-fusion-measurement]] on a finite-dimensional fusion space $H$,
and let $\psi\in H$ be a unit vector. The channel probabilities
$p_a=\|P_a\psi\|^2$ are nonnegative and sum to one. If $p_a>0$, the
conditional branch is the unit vector $P_a\psi/\sqrt{p_a}$. If $p_a=0$,
then $P_a\psi=0$ and no normalized conditional state is defined.

If the surviving channel is $a$ with coefficient $\alpha$, normalization gives $|\alpha|=1$, so its conditional vector is $\alpha|a\rangle$, representing the same pure state as $|a\rangle$. This checks both zero-coefficient boundary cases without fixing a global phase.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and $U:H\to H$ a unitary. Let $\theta\in\mathbb R$, and suppose the model separately grants controlled access to both $U$ and $e^{i\theta}U$. There is a normalized eigenvector $\phi$ with $U\phi=\mu\phi$ and $|\mu|=1$. Let $C=Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the control qubit with ordered computational basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$; define $|\pm\rangle=(|0\rangle\pm|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and prepare $(|0\rangle+\overline\mu|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with target $\phi$. The two joint effects are $E_\pm=|\pm\rangle\langle\pm|\otimes I_H$. The $E_+$ outcome has probability $1$ after $C(U)$ and $\cos^2(\theta/2)$ after $C(e^{i\theta}U)$. Thus the two controlled maps give different outcome laws exactly when $\theta\notin2\pi\mathbb Z$; when $\theta\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, the controlled maps coincide. This is a mathematical witness; it does not assert that controlled access or the witness-state preparation is free.

Let $G_{\rm Fib}$ be the fixed Fibonacci SU(2) alphabet with a supplied finite
base-net certificate of radius $0<\eta_0<64^{-2}$ and maximum word length
$L_0$. For every exact target $S\in SU(2)$ and rational
$0<\varepsilon\le\eta_0$, let
$$\eta_{j+1}=64\eta_j^{3/2},\qquad J=\min\{j\ge0:\eta_j\le\varepsilon\}.$$
The ideal SK recursion returns a normalized braid word $W$ with
$\|S-W\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon$ and length at most $L_0 5^J$; hence its
length is $O(\log^{\log_{3/2}5}(1/\varepsilon))=O(\log^{3.97}(1/\varepsilon))$.
If each real and imaginary gate coordinate is supplied by its minimal
polynomial and rational isolating interval with the endpoint/root conditions
of the published finite-precision theorem, the base certificate is fixed,
and $S$ has a polynomial-time Cauchy name with query cost at most $(b+1)^c$,
the finite implementation additionally has the bit-time bound
$O((N+s_\varepsilon)^{c+10})$ from the cited theorem, where
$N=\lceil\log_2(2/\varepsilon)\rceil$ and $s_\varepsilon$ is the binary
encoding length of the rational tolerance. The lifted physical braid carries
$(R_1z^{-1})^k$ and that phase is not part of the normalized error.

$$\bigl(L_{\rm in},\ N_{\rm any},\ |b|,\ N_{\rm prep},\ N_{\rm anc},\ N_{\rm meas},\ B_{\rm out},\ b_{\max},\ t_{\rm cl},\ T_H,\ \epsilon_{\rm op},\epsilon_{\rm tr},\epsilon_{\rm meas},\ell_{\rm leak},\ p_{\rm leak},\ N_{\rm phase},\ t_{\rm phase},\ \mathsf C_{\rm circ},\ N_{\rm nonoracle}\bigr).$$
Here $L_{\rm in}$ is the complete finite classical input-description bit
length, including the declared task, state/preparation descriptions when
classically encoded, and tolerance descriptions; a directly supplied quantum
input is not assumed to have a finite classical coordinate description;
$N_{\rm any}$ is the number of ordered simple-charge strand labels in the
fusion-space instance; and $|b|$ is the number of braid-generator occurrences
(inverse generators count as one). $N_{\rm prep}$ counts elementary
operations in the declared preparation procedure, while $N_{\rm anc}$ counts

input with no preparation interface, $N_{\rm prep}$ is “not applicable”, not

(zero if none, or “not applicable” if no physical ancilla model is supplied).
$N_{\rm meas}$ is the number of fusion measurements,
and $B_{\rm out}$ is the total bit length of their classical outcome record
under its declared finite encoding (zero when no measurement occurs). The
largest unary precision query to a certified matrix name is $b_{\max}$; $t_{\rm cl}$
is the classical bit time used by search and postprocessing. $T_H$ is the total

it is “not applicable” for an abstract braid-only model without Hamiltonian

may overlap $N_{\rm prep}$ and $N_{\rm anc}$; they are separate reported
resources, not disjoint summands to be added. Without a circuit implementation
interface, $\mathsf C_{\rm circ}$ and $N_{\rm nonoracle}$ are “not applicable”.
Classical
input bit cost follows [[def-qa-classical-bit-cost]] and finite nonoracle
gates follow [[def-qa-nonoracle-gate-cost]]. An inapplicable coordinate is
marked “not applicable”; it is not assigned value zero. Unless an interface

matrix precision, measurement, Hamiltonian time, search step, or phase

The code and leakage components of $B_jE-E\widehat G_j$ each have norm at most $\delta/2$: they are $E(E^*B_jE-\widehat G_j)$ and $(I-P)B_jE$. Their sum therefore has norm at most $\delta$.

The minimum defining $\delta$ gives $M\delta\le\varepsilon/2$, including equality of its two candidates. By [F2], SK length, B6 search work, measurement and phase correction remain separate costs.
